verdicts.threatModel: No attacker: links.rs:28 FEEDBACK is a compile-time &'static str naming the GitHub new-issue page of Orthic-Labs/ember, with no untrusted input feeding it.
verdicts.reachability: Reached only via LINKS entry app.feedback (links.rs:24) and url_of, then links::open hands the string to the host open_url service, which launches the user's browser; nothing is fetched or executed by Ember.
verdicts.impact: None. A browser navigation to an HTML issue form is not a downloaded binary, so the digest-pinning rule has nothing to pin; integrity is provided by HTTPS to github.com.
verdicts.rationale: The scanner matched an https URL literal; the value is a hyperlink opened in a browser, never downloaded or executed by the app.

verdicts.threatModel: No attacker model applies to the GITHUB constant at links.rs:12: it is a hard-coded repository homepage URL with no external data source.
verdicts.reachability: Used by the Help menu entry app.github (links.rs:22) and the About dialog list (panels/dialogs.rs:1183), both passing it to links::open, which only asks the OS to open a browser tab.
verdicts.impact: None. The repository landing page is browsed by the user, not retrieved as an executable; there is no binary whose digest could be pinned.
verdicts.rationale: Hyperlink literal misclassified as a binary download by a URL-pattern scanner.

verdicts.threatModel: No threat exists at links.rs:49: the line is an assert inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests that checks every LINKS entry starts with the https:// prefix.
verdicts.reachability: Compiled only under cfg(test) (links.rs:42); it is never part of a shipped binary and performs no network access at all.
verdicts.impact: None. The line is itself a defensive check that link URLs use TLS; it downloads nothing and cannot weaken any binary supply chain.
verdicts.rationale: The scanner matched the substring https:// inside a test assertion string literal, not a URL being fetched.

verdicts.threatModel: No attacker controls APP_PAGE at links.rs:10; it is a static project-page string for the Ember fork, fixed at build time.
verdicts.reachability: Consumed by the app.website menu link (links.rs:21) and the About dialog (panels/dialogs.rs:1182); both route through links::open to the host browser launcher, with no fetch inside Ember.
verdicts.impact: None. Opening a project web page in the user's browser carries no binary-integrity risk, so a content digest is inapplicable.
verdicts.rationale: Static web-page constant flagged only because it is an https URL; the test at links.rs:53 even asserts it equals GITHUB.

verdicts.threatModel: WEBSITE at links.rs:8 is a fixed organisation profile URL (github.com/Orthic-Labs); no untrusted party supplies or alters it at runtime.
verdicts.reachability: Reached from the app.artcraft menu entry (links.rs:23), the About dialog (panels/dialogs.rs:1184) and as the url_of fallback in menus.rs:1871, always ending in a browser open request.
verdicts.impact: None. It names an organisation landing page for a human to browse; Ember never downloads content from it, so pinning a digest is meaningless.
verdicts.rationale: URL-shaped constant mistaken for a binary download; its only sink is the browser launcher.

verdicts.threatModel: DISCORD at links.rs:6 is a legacy-named constant pointing to the GitHub issues list; it is compiled in and has no attacker-controlled source.
verdicts.reachability: Used by the app.discord menu item (links.rs:20) and the About dialog button (panels/dialogs.rs:1175-1178), which call links::open to show the page in the browser.
verdicts.impact: None. An issues listing page is navigated, not downloaded or executed, so the absence of an immutable digest has no security consequence.
verdicts.rationale: The scanner's binary-pin rule fires on any https literal; this one is a community link.

verdicts.threatModel: No attacker: menubar.rs:1456 is the opening of a raw-string GPX fixture inside the auto_tag_from_tracklog unit test, and http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1 is an XML namespace identifier.
verdicts.reachability: The string is written to a temp file by std::fs::write in test code (menubar.rs:1454-1458) and parsed as a tracklog; XML namespace URIs are never dereferenced by the parser.
verdicts.impact: None. A namespace URI is an opaque identifier, nothing is downloaded, and the code is test-only, so no binary supply-chain exposure exists.
verdicts.rationale: Namespace URI inside a test GPX document matched the URL regex.

verdicts.threatModel: SAM_HELP at panels/dialogs.rs:1425 is a constant documentation anchor (ai-masks.md#getting-the-model); no untrusted input reaches it.
verdicts.reachability: Shown as hover text and opened with links::open from the SAM model dialog (dialogs.rs:1487-1490, 1539-1542); it opens a Markdown help page in the browser and does not fetch the model.
verdicts.impact: None at this line. The help page is read by a human; the actual model download path (Segmenter mirrors) is separate code not referenced by this candidate, so no unpinned binary is fetched here.
verdicts.rationale: Help-page hyperlink flagged by URL pattern; it is documentation, not the download source.

verdicts.threatModel: At panels/right.rs:667 the URL is formatted from the photo's own GPS latitude/longitude as {:.6} floats; an attacker crafting EXIF can only choose two numbers.
verdicts.reachability: Triggered when the user clicks Show on Map; the format! output goes to links::open (right.rs:668) which opens openstreetmap.org in the browser. Float formatting cannot inject path or scheme characters.
verdicts.impact: None. It is a map page navigation, not a binary download, and numeric formatting removes any URL-injection vector; the scheme and host are fixed to https://www.openstreetmap.org.
verdicts.rationale: Map hyperlink built from numeric coordinates, misread as an unpinned binary URL.

verdicts.threatModel: tests_panels.rs:2017 is a one-line GPX fixture string in a test module; its topografix URI is the GPX XML namespace, not a resource location used by code.
verdicts.reachability: Written to a per-process temp directory by std::fs::write in test code and parsed by the tracklog importer; XML namespaces are not fetched, and the file is excluded from release builds.
verdicts.impact: None. No network retrieval occurs and the code ships in no product binary, so the binary-pinning concern cannot apply.
verdicts.rationale: Test-fixture XML namespace matched the scanner's URL heuristic.

verdicts.threatModel: docs/showcase/run.py:13 opens sys.argv[1], the JSON-lines script path the developer passes on the command line; the only actor choosing that path is the local user who already has full filesystem access.
verdicts.reachability: The script is a developer showcase driver (docs/showcase, documented in CLAUDE.md as run.py file.jsonl) invoked by hand; it has no network, service or privileged entry point that could supply the argument.
verdicts.impact: None. Reading a file the invoking user names grants no capability across a trust boundary; the file is only parsed as JSON control requests sent to the user's own localhost:7980 app.
verdicts.rationale: Path-traversal rule assumes attacker-controlled path data, but argv of a local CLI tool is the operator's own input.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered: tampering with the Flathub remote used at flatpak-bundle.sh:20 to install the freedesktop runtime/SDK during release bundling.
verdicts.reachability: FLATHUB is passed to flatpak remote-add (line 55) and --runtime-repo (line 62) in the release workflow (release.yml:274). The .flatpakrepo file carries Flathub's GPG key and flatpak verifies every OSTree commit signature against it.
verdicts.impact: None beyond normal trust in Flathub. Runtimes are integrity-verified by flatpak's GPG-signed OSTree commits, and a repo descriptor is not a binary; pinning a file digest would add nothing over signature verification.
verdicts.rationale: A remote descriptor URL over HTTPS whose content is signature-verified by flatpak, not an unverified binary download.

verdicts.threatModel: package.sh:12 is a shell comment documenting that nfpm is needed and where its homepage is; there is no code and no attacker-influenced data on the line.
verdicts.reachability: Comments are not executed. The real nfpm install in CI is release.yml:209-211, which downloads a version-pinned release (NFPM_VERSION 2.47.0), a separate location from this candidate.
verdicts.impact: None. A documentation link in a usage comment cannot download or run anything.
verdicts.rationale: Scanner matched a URL inside a '#' comment.

verdicts.threatModel: Supply-chain threat: whoever can alter the AppImage/appimagetool 'continuous' GitHub release (compromised upstream maintainer or release asset) substitutes the appimagetool executable that package.sh:113 downloads and then runs.
verdicts.reachability: Reached in the release workflow: release.yml:223 runs packaging/linux/package.sh with no APPIMAGETOOL set, so when appimagetool is not on PATH the script curls the mutable 'continuous' asset (package.sh:113), chmod +x's it and executes it to build the published AppImage.
verdicts.impact: A replaced tool would execute on the release runner and could embed a modified runtime into the shipped Ember AppImage. Exploitation requires compromise of the upstream project, not of Ember, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a demonstrated vulnerability; TLS protects only transport.
verdicts.rationale: Mutable 'continuous' tag plus no sha256 check on an executable run in the release pipeline; pin a tagged release and verify its digest.

verdicts.threatModel: package.sh:89 only checks `command -v nfpm` and prints an error message containing the nfpm install-docs URL; no data from any attacker is involved.
verdicts.reachability: The URL appears inside an echo string sent to stderr before exit 1; the script never fetches it. In CI nfpm is pre-installed from a pinned version at release.yml:209-211.
verdicts.impact: None. Printing a help URL in an error message has no integrity or execution effect.
verdicts.rationale: URL inside an error-message string, not a download.

verdicts.threatModel: render-icons.py:39 builds an SVG wrapper whose xmlns attribute is the W3C SVG namespace; the only variable data is the base64 of a locally rendered PNG.
verdicts.reachability: embedded_svg is a local build helper that concatenates strings into an SVG document; the namespace http://www.w3.org/2000/svg is an identifier never requested over the network.
verdicts.impact: None. No download occurs and the namespace identifier has no content to pin.
verdicts.rationale: W3C SVG namespace literal matched the URL rule.

verdicts.threatModel: sign.ps1:9 is in the comment-based help block (.DESCRIPTION), giving an example Azure Trusted Signing endpoint; no runtime value is set here.
verdicts.reachability: Lines 1-19 are a PowerShell <# #> help comment and are never executed; the real endpoint comes from the AZURE_SIGNING_ENDPOINT environment secret at line 84.
verdicts.impact: None. Example text in documentation fetches nothing.
verdicts.rationale: Example URL inside a help comment.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered at sign.ps1:67: an on-path attacker interfering with the plain-http DigiCert RFC 3161 timestamp request made by signtool /tr.
verdicts.reachability: Used only when signing with WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE; signtool sends a hash to the TSA and receives a timestamp token. Line 91 then runs signtool verify /pa on the result.
verdicts.impact: None material. RFC 3161 tokens are signed by the TSA and validated by signtool, so tampering yields a failed signature/verify rather than a forged timestamp; nothing executable is downloaded. HTTP is DigiCert's documented endpoint.
verdicts.rationale: A timestamp authority URL is not a binary download; token integrity comes from the TSA's signature.

verdicts.threatModel: Supply-chain threat: a compromise or account takeover of the Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client NuGet package lets the attacker publish a new latest version that sign.ps1:77 downloads without a version or hash.
verdicts.reachability: Reached when Azure signing secrets are set (sign.ps1:49-50) via package.ps1:116/143. The unversioned v2 package URL resolves to the latest release; the extracted Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll is loaded into signtool (line 89) in a process whose environment holds AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET.
verdicts.impact: A malicious DLL would run inside the signing step with the Azure client secret available and could sign arbitrary binaries or exfiltrate the credential. Requires upstream package compromise, so it is a hardening gap; pinning a version and checking the nupkg sha256 closes it.
verdicts.rationale: Unpinned latest-version download of code that is executed with signing credentials present.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered at sign.ps1:88: tampering with the http Microsoft ACS timestamp service used in the Azure Trusted Signing branch.
verdicts.reachability: signtool /tr posts a digest to timestamp.acs.microsoft.com and embeds the returned RFC 3161 token; signtool verify /pa at line 91 validates the resulting signatures.
verdicts.impact: None material. Microsoft's TSA signs its tokens, so an altered response fails validation; no file is downloaded or executed, so a content digest cannot apply. This is Microsoft's documented Trusted Signing timestamp URL.
verdicts.rationale: Timestamp endpoint, distinct from a binary download; integrity rests on the TSA signature.

verdicts.threatModel: test-install-folder.ps1:41 registers the WiX v4 XML namespace with an XmlNamespaceManager for XPath queries over the local lightcraft.wxs; no attacker input is involved.
verdicts.reachability: AddNamespace binds the prefix 'w' to the URI string for SelectNodes; .NET never dereferences namespace URIs, and the script runs only as a local installer test.
verdicts.impact: None. Nothing is downloaded, so there is no binary to pin.
verdicts.rationale: XML namespace identifier flagged as a download URL.

verdicts.threatModel: test-install-folder.ps1:55 is the root element of a generated WiX probe document in a here-string; the xmlns value is a schema identifier with no attacker involvement.
verdicts.reachability: The here-string is written as WiX source for a test package built by the local WiX toolchain; the WiX compiler treats the namespace as an identifier and performs no network fetch.
verdicts.impact: None. No retrieval of any binary occurs from this URI in a test-only script.
verdicts.rationale: WiX namespace in a test XML template matched the URL rule.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered: a modified craft-fonts repository serving altered font files to the build cloned at build-native.mjs:29.
verdicts.reachability: The clone is immediately followed by `git checkout 8dcdacd5153e64560d109541a47d806f26f048c0` (line 31), and the build fails if that checkout fails (line 32); only the pinned commit's tree is used as CRAFT_FONTS_DIR.
verdicts.impact: None. A full git commit SHA is an immutable content address over the whole tree, which is exactly the pin the rule asks for; an attacker cannot make different content match that commit.
verdicts.rationale: The scanner looked only at the clone line and missed the pinned-commit checkout two lines below.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered: a substituted face_landmarker.task model behind the ARTIFACT_URL at line 43.
verdicts.reachability: The script does not download ARTIFACT_URL; inspect() reads a local file argument and rejects it unless length equals ARTIFACT_BYTES and SHA-256 equals ARTIFACT_SHA256 (lines 347-350). The URL is only echoed in the report (line 385).
verdicts.impact: None. An immutable digest (line 42) and byte length (line 41) are pinned and enforced before parsing, so a tampered artifact is refused.
verdicts.rationale: The digest sits on the adjacent line; the scanner missed it.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered: an altered metadata_schema.fbs at the METADATA_SCHEMA_URL formatted at line 51.
verdicts.reachability: The URL embeds a fixed git revision (line 48), and the local schema file passed in is checked against METADATA_SCHEMA_BYTES and METADATA_SCHEMA_SHA256 (lines 49-50, 355-358) before use; the script never fetches the URL itself.
verdicts.impact: None. Commit-pinned URL plus enforced SHA-256 and size make substitution detectable and fatal.
verdicts.rationale: Pinned revision and sha256 are both present; rule fired on the URL text alone.
